name: Surface Splatting and Lighting
text:
# Surface Splatting and Lighting
## Overview
Surface Splatting and Lighting is a family of rendering techniques that convert unstructured point clouds into continuous, shaded surfaces by projecting points as splats into a rendering pipeline [G]. It solves sparse dot cloud aliasing and transparency artifacts by assigning each point sample an extent drawn as a small oriented primitive (a splat) carrying a radially decreasing reconstruction kernel [G]. It differs from its parent [EWA Splatting](1069-ewa-splatting.md) by using screen-aligned spherical impostors with isotropic linear falloff rather than anisotropic, correctly band-limited EWA footprints, trading accurate filtering for a formulation that requires no per-point normals or radii [G].

## Shared principles
The family shares the core mechanism of treating each point sample as a local surface patch that is rasterized as a primitive (typically a point sprite or quadrilateral) to cover the area where the underlying surface is expected to exist [G]. The rendering pipeline accumulates surface attributes (color, normal, depth) from overlapping splats to reconstruct a continuous signal [G]. Lighting is applied either during the accumulation pass (if normals are available per-splat) or in a deferred screen-space pass using the accumulated normal buffer [G].

## Subtopics

### [Deferred Surface Splatting](1072-deferred-surface-splatting.md)
[Deferred Surface Splatting](#1072-deferred-surface-splatting.md) converts unstructured point clouds into continuous, shaded surfaces by projecting points as splats into a [deferred rendering pipeline](#10584-deferred-rendering-pipeline.md) [G]. It differs from forward [splatting](#23-splatting.md) siblings by decoupling geometric projection from lighting calculation, accumulating attributes into a G-buffer for a final screen-space pass [G]. Choose it when handling heavy overlap or multiple light sources efficiently without re-projecting geometry [G].

### [Phong Splatting](2802-phong-splatting.md)
[Phong Splatting](#2802-phong-splatting.md) assigns a linearly varying normal field to each elliptical splat, enabling per-pixel [Phong shading](#1853-phong-shading.md) without surface connectivity [G]. It differs from isotropic kernel siblings by using elliptical splats with projectively correct per-pixel parameterization, trading simplicity for superior visual quality and exact depth values [G]. Choose it when smooth, curvature-aware shading is required over simple point sprites [G].

### EWA Surface Splatting
**Definition:** A method where EWA volume splats reduce to surface splats suitable for high-quality iso-surface rendering by flattening the 3D Gaussian kernel along the volume gradient [S1, unofficial].
**Step:** For each point in object-space, quadrilaterals texture-mapped with a Gaussian texture are deformed to result in the correct screen-space EWA splat after projection [S1, unofficial].

## Background
The concept of EWA surface splats was derived by Ren et al. [Ren et al. 2002] as an object-space formulation of EWA volume splats, describing an efficient implementation on graphics hardware [S1, unofficial]. The technique involves deforming quadrilaterals texture-mapped with a Gaussian texture to result in the correct screen-space EWA splat after projection [S1, unofficial]. This approach allows for high-quality iso-surface rendering by flattening the 3D Gaussian kernel along the volume gradient [S1, unofficial].
